summary: The bill repeals the enhanced oil recovery tax credit under section 43 and bars new carbon capture facilities from claiming the 45Q credit for using captured carbon oxide as a tertiary injectant in oil wells.

scores.thoughts: The bill repeals the enhanced oil recovery credit (section 43) and restricts the carbon oxide sequestration credit (section 45Q) when used for enhanced oil recovery. Both changes eliminate tax expenditures that function as government subsidies, directly reducing federal spending on these activities.

By repealing tax credits under sections 43 and 45Q for enhanced oil recovery, the bill removes tax preferences for corporations in the oil sector. This has the effect of increasing the net tax burden on those activities rather than lowering taxes.
The bill contains no provisions related to healthcare, insurance, medical providers, or public/private coverage models.
The bill contains no provisions related to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The bill contains no provisions related to immigration, border security, visas, or pathways to citizenship.
The bill contains no provisions related to reproductive health, abortion access, or funding restrictions.
The bill contains no provisions related to military budgets, defense spending, or armed forces.

The bill targets and eliminates tax credits specifically used for enhanced oil recovery, a process that supports continued fossil fuel extraction. This removes a subsidy for oil production and aligns with efforts to reduce support for carbon-intensive activities.
The bill contains no provisions related to welfare programs, food assistance, unemployment benefits, or other safety-net spending.
The bill contains no provisions related to schools, education funding, school choice, or federal education policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.
The bill contains no provisions related to sentencing, policing, incarceration, or criminal justice reform.
The bill contains no provisions related to tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export policy.
By repealing tax credits that constitute spending, the bill reduces federal outlays and thereby contributes to deficit reduction and debt management.
The bill contains no provisions related to LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.

The bill contains no provisions related to voting access, election administration, or campaign finance.

The bill contains no provisions related to unions, collective bargaining, worker protections, or employment law.
